Der Wert der Einfuhren sank von 15,0 Milliarden auf gut 0,5 Milliarden Euro. Die deutschen Ausfuhren nach Russland brachen im selben Zeitraum um 73,1 Prozent ein - von gut 12,7 auf 3,4 Milliarden Euro. Die Sanktionen der Europäischen Union haben die Handelsstruktur grundlegend verändert. Waren im Vorkriegszeitraum vor allem Erdöl und Erdgas die wichtigsten Importgüter, sind es nun Nahrungs- und Futtermittel, Metalle und chemische Erzeugnisse. Bei den Exporten dominieren inzwischen pharmazeutische Erzeugnisse, die mehr als 40 Prozent der Lieferungen ausmachen. "LANGE ZEIT EINE SCHWERE HYPOTHEK" Die wirtschaftliche Entflechtung zeigt sich auch bei den Unternehmen. Die Zahl der von Russland aus kontrollierten Firmen in Deutschland sank von 229 im Jahr 2021 auf 76 im Jahr 2024. Ihr Umsatz brach von knapp 25,4 auf 8,4 Milliarden Euro ein. Umgekehrt ging die Zahl der von deutschen Investoren kontrollierten Unternehmen in Russland im selben Zeitraum von 481 auf 290 zurück. Der dort erzielte Jahresumsatz fiel von rund 38 auf 13 Milliarden Euro. "Die Zahlen unterstreichen die umfassende Entkopplung der deutschen und russischen Wirtschaft seit Beginn des russischen Angriffskriegs gegen die Ukraine", betonte der Ost-Ausschuss der Deutschen Wirtschaft. Unter den deutschen Handelspartnern weltweit sei Russland binnen fünf Jahren von Rang 13 auf Rang 49 abgerutscht. "Die gute Nachricht ist: Der deutsche Osthandel konnte den Ausfall Russlands kompensieren – ein Zeichen für die wirtschaftliche Dynamik der gesamten Region und die Flexibilität deutscher Unternehmen", hieß es. In den vergangenen Monaten seien die Tätigkeit und der Rückzug ausländischer Unternehmen aus Russland weiter erschwert worden, etwa durch neue Eingriffe in Eigentumsrechte und Gewinntransfers. "Diese fehlende Rechtssicherheit in Russland und der damit verbundene massive Vertrauensverlust wird auf lange Zeit eine schwere Hypothek für die deutsch-russischen Wirtschaftsbeziehungen bleiben", so der Ost-Ausschuss. WENIGER STUDIENANFÄNGER Der Austausch zwischen beiden Ländern ist auch auf anderer Ebene stark zurückgegangen. Wegen des bestehenden Direktflugverbots ging im ersten Halbjahr die Zahl der an deutschen Hauptverkehrsflughäfen startenden wie auch der dort landenden Fluggäste mit Direktverbindung nach und von Russland gegen null. Mit letztbekanntem Streckenziel Russland hoben noch gut 39.900 Fluggäste von Deutschland ab – beispielsweise mit Umstieg in der Türkei oder anderen Drittstaaten ohne Direktflugverbot. Das waren 95,9 Prozent weniger als im ersten Halbjahr 2019, also vor den pandemiebedingten Einschränkungen des Flugverkehrs. Zudem hat sich die Wanderungsbewegung umgekehrt: Im ersten Halbjahr zogen mehr russische Staatsangehörige aus Deutschland fort, als hierher kamen. Auch die Zahl russischer Studienanfänger in Deutschland hat sich von 2021 bis 2025 um 40 Prozent verringert. Seit dem Beginn des russischen Angriffskriegs im Februar 2022 hat die EU in 21 Paketen weitreichende Sanktionen verhängt. Diese betreffen unter anderem den Handel, den Finanzsektor und den Flugverkehr.

item.title: Tunisia targets 16% renewable power share in 2027, plans 1,600 MW of new capacity
item.description: Tunisia aims to increase the share of renewable energy in its electricity mix to 16% in 2027, from 12% this year, driven by plans to develop around 1,600 megawatts of renewable energy capacity, the finance law seen by Reuters showed.
item.dc:creator: Tarek Amara
item.content:encoded: Tunisia aims to increase the share of renewable energy in its electricity mix to 16% in 2027, from 12% this year, driven by plans to develop around 1,600 megawatts of renewable energy capacity, the finance law seen by Reuters showed. Of the planned capacity, around 1,100 MW will be offered to international investors under concession and licensing projects, while the remaining 500 MW will be allocated to self-generation projects. Under the concession projects, Tunisia expects a 198 MW renewable energy project at the Khnabna site and a 77 MW wind farm to enter service. Construction is also set to begin on a 300 MW solar power plant in Bazma, in the southern governorate of Kebili, equipped with battery storage. Separately, the government plans to install around 515 MW of renewable energy capacity under the sixth round of the licensing scheme. The Finance bill did not provide further details on the projects. Tunisia is seeking to strengthen its energy security after a difficult summer in which residents faced repeated power outages amid electricity supply shortages that left demand unmet and sparked protests. Tunisia, mostly dependent on gas-fired power, aims to generate 35% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.

item.title: Prabowo accuses MSCI of trying to intimidate Indonesia after market rout
item.description: Global index provider MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia but the country would not be afraid, President Prabowo Subianto told his cabinet on Wednesday, striking a combative tone in his first public reaction to last week's downgrade warning.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global index provider MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia but the country would not be afraid, President Prabowo Subianto told his cabinet on Wednesday, striking a combative tone in his first public reaction to last week's [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"downgrade "][USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"warning"]. MSCI ratcheted up the pressure on Jakarta by announcing that it could demote Indonesia's equities to[USN:L6N46208E TEXT:" "standalone" market status"], claiming the country had not done enough to [USN:L4N46509U TEXT:"crack down on coordinated trading practices"] in its stock market. The surprise announcement triggered a [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"record-breaking two-day stock market rout"], with a downgrade threatening to cause massive capital flight and cut the $1.5 trillion G20 economy off from major emerging market index flows. "The MSCI...intended to intimidate us," Prabowo told a gathering of his cabinet that was broadcast on the government's official YouTube channel. "I simply say to the MSCI: the Indonesian nation fears no one and will not be cowed," he continued, adding: "We possess strength, we have courage, we are willing to make sacrifices, and we refuse to surrender." MSCI, in an emailed reply to a request for comment, said that its decisions follow transparent and rules-based methodologies. "MSCI will continue to monitor developments in the Indonesian market and engage with market participants and authorities," it said. Prabowo, a former special forces commander, has often used strongly nationalist language since coming to power in 2024, suggesting foreign powers were determined to destabilise Indonesia, the world's largest Muslim majority country and a global commodities powerhouse. His speech on Wednesday also made reference to outside interference in Indonesia, though he did not elaborate. Other senior Indonesian political figures have also reacted strongly to MSCI's warning. On Tuesday, former Indonesian trade minister M. Lutfi claimed on his Instagram account that Singapore sovereign wealth funds Temasek and GIC were involved in pressuring MSCI to issue the warning to Indonesia. An official from Temasek described Lutfi's comments as "patently untrue" while GIC also rejected the charge, DealStreet Asia reported on Wednesday. Last week, senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto also said there was "a big question mark" over why MSCI had not discussed the possible downgrade during meetings with Indonesian officials in Bangkok just days before. Hanif Dhakiri of the National Awakening Party, who sits on the parliamentary committee overseeing finance affairs, demanded that MSCI's methodology be transparent, objective and consistently applied across countries. "We should not be defensive in the face of criticism, but neither should we accept judgements without examining their basis and objectivity," he told Reuters. Said Abdullah, a lawmaker from the opposition PDI-P party, said on Sunday Indonesia should take MSCI's concerns seriously, but argued that the index provider's judgements should not be beyond scrutiny. "MSCI's executives are not prophets delivering divine revelations, like apostles writing sacred texts, who can claim a monopoly on flawless truth," Said added.

item.title: El Barça denuncia ante la UEFA un tifo de los hinchas del PSG con el lema "Una masacre a la parisina"
item.description: El Barcelona denunció ante la UEFA un tifo exhibido por los hinchas del Paris Saint-Germain antes de su partido de la Liga de Campeones, informó el club el miércoles.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: El Barcelona denunció ante la UEFA un tifo exhibido por los hinchas del Paris Saint-Germain antes de su partido de la Liga de Campeones, informó el club el miércoles. Antes del encuentro del martes en el Parque de los Príncipes, los aficionados del PSG desplegaron un tifo con el lema "Una masacre a la parisina", que mostraba a una figura enmascarada con una camiseta del PSG cortando con una motosierra el escudo del Barcelona. La imagen hacía referencia a la película de terror de 1974 "The Texas Chain Saw Massacre". Un portavoz del Barcelona dijo a Reuters que, una vez terminado el partido, el club denunció el contenido del tifo ante el delegado de la UEFA, así como diversos cánticos ofensivos que se escucharon desde las gradas. El PSG había aprobado el tifo antes del partido, según L'Équipe. El club no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. El artículo 16 del reglamento disciplinario de la UEFA establece que "el uso de gestos, palabras, objetos o cualquier otro medio para transmitir un mensaje provocador inapropiado para un evento deportivo" puede dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias. La sanción habitual por una primera infracción de esta naturaleza es una multa de 10.000 euros (11.221 dólares). (1 dólar = 0,8912 euros)

item.title: El Gobierno francés se enfrenta a una nueva prueba ante la movilización de los chalecos amarillos
item.description: El movimiento de los chalecos amarillos de Francia presentó los planes para una gran marcha por París el sábado, lo que supone una nueva prueba de fuego para el Gobierno tras los disturbios y saqueos del pasado fin de semana, que sacudieron la confianza en su capacidad para mantener el orden.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: El movimiento de los chalecos amarillos de Francia presentó los planes para una gran marcha por París el sábado, lo que supone una nueva prueba de fuego para el Gobierno tras los disturbios y saqueos del pasado fin de semana, que sacudieron la confianza en su capacidad para mantener el orden. El primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu, tenía previsto reunirse este miércoles con los líderes sindicales para buscar formas de calmar una de las peores crisis a las que se ha enfrentado Francia en los últimos años y evitar que se repita la violencia que se extendió por las ciudades francesas el 17 de octubre. Un representante del movimiento de los "Gilets Jaunes" (chalecos amarillos), un grupo de base no vinculado a los sindicatos, presentó los planes para una marcha por el centro de París, incluyendo zonas que fueron saqueadas hace apenas unos días. Los colectivos estudiantiles también han convocado manifestaciones para ese mismo día con el fin de presionar por sus reivindicaciones de una mayor inversión en educación. Los activistas de los chalecos amarillos pretenden reactivar su campaña, surgida en 2018, contra el aumento del costo de la vida y el deterioro de los servicios públicos. LOS INVERSIONISTAS SE PREOCUPAN, AUMENTAN LOS COSTOS DE FINANCIAMIENTO Las manifestaciones del pasado fin de semana degeneraron rápidamente en violencia desenfrenada, especialmente en París, Marsella, Lyon y Limoges, y la policía, desbordada, tardó horas en controlar la situación. Como muestra de la preocupación de los inversionistas por la situación, los costos de financiamiento del Gobierno francés han aumentado considerablemente esta semana, lo que ha elevado el [USN:L6N4670OA TEXT:"rendimiento de los bonos"] de referencia a 10 años hasta el 5%, su nivel más alto desde julio de 2002. Los analistas señalaron que a los mercados les preocupa que los disturbios puedan complicar los esfuerzos del Gobierno por sanear las maltrechas finanzas públicas en un momento en el que las presiones presupuestarias ya van en aumento. El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, ha anunciado que se reunirá con los servicios de inteligencia este jueves, antes de las nuevas protestas. Los ministros del Gobierno han prometido una operación de seguridad considerablemente reforzada tras reconocer las deficiencias en su respuesta inicial, y se espera que se desplieguen soldados junto con más efectivos policiales. En una carta dirigida a los sindicatos antes de la reunión del miércoles, Lecornu señaló que las conversaciones deberían centrarse en garantizar "la indispensable libertad de manifestación", que, según él, algunos intentaban restringir al asociarla con "actos inaceptables". Los principales sindicatos franceses han convocado por separado una movilización a nivel nacional para el 5 de noviembre. "Hay una ira enorme y legítima, y la respuesta a esa situación no es la represión. Es una respuesta política. Eso es lo que le diré hoy al primer ministro", dijo Sophie Binet, líder del sindicato CGT, a la emisora RTL. OPOSICIÓN POLÍTICA MIENTRAS EL GOBIERNO TIENE DIFICULTADES Una segunda noche consecutiva de toques de queda locales transcurrió sin incidentes graves en las zonas afectadas por los disturbios, lo que supuso un respiro para el Gobierno mientras se preparaba para nuevas manifestaciones. Los disturbios han desencadenado una respuesta negativa política ante las elecciones presidenciales del año que viene, en las que los candidatos de la extrema derecha y la izquierda obtienen buenos resultados en las encuestas. "El Gobierno ha perdido el control de todo", dijo la líder de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen a la emisora Franceinfo. La formación de izquierda Francia Insumisa (LFI, por sus siglas en francés), a la que los ministros han acusado de avivar los disturbios, criticó los planes de desplegar militares en las calles de París. "Los manifestantes no son enemigos internos. El Gobierno francés no debe entrar en guerra contra su propio pueblo", dijo el grupo parlamentario de LFI en un comunicado. Las protestas en otros países europeos, entre ellos Italia y Albania, han agravado la preocupación de que la indignación por el nivel de vida corra el riesgo de extenderse por todo el continente, en un momento en que muchos países, incluido Francia, se enfrentan a dificultades presupuestarias. Italia aprobó el martes una serie de medidas de seguridad, entre las que se incluyen un nuevo delito de participación violenta en una manifestación y penas más severas para los alborotadores, en respuesta a los disturbios del pasado fin de semana.

item.title: Barcelona report 'Paris-style massacre' fan display to UEFA after PSG game
item.description: Barcelona reported a tifo shown by Paris St Germain supporters before their Champions League game to UEFA, the club said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Barcelona reported a tifo shown by Paris St Germain supporters before their Champions League game to UEFA, the club said on Wednesday. Ahead of their Champions League clash at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday, PSG fans unveiled the banner display that read 'a Paris-style massacre', depicting a masked figure in a PSG shirt taking a chainsaw to the Barcelona badge. The motif was a reference to the 1974 horror film "The Texas Chain Saw Massacre". A Barcelona spokesperson told Reuters that after the match ended, they reported the content of the tifo to the UEFA match delegate, as well as various offensive songs that were heard from the stands. The tifo was approved by PSG before the match, according to L'Equipe. The club did not immediately respond to a request for comment. UEFA disciplinary regulations state in article 16 (2e) that "the use of gestures, words, objects or any other means to transmit a provocative message that is not fit for a sports event" may result in disciplinary measures. The standard sanction for a first offence of this nature is a €10,000 ($11,221) fine. ($1 = 0.8912 euros)

item.title: Philip Morris tops quarterly estimates on nicotine pouch and tobacco prices
item.description: Philip Morris International PM.N beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter sales and profit on Wednesday, helped by strong demand for its Zyn nicotine pouches and by higher cigarette prices, and kept its full-year profit forecast intact.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philip Morris International <PM.N> beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter sales and profit on Wednesday, helped by strong demand for its Zyn nicotine pouches and by higher cigarette prices, and kept its full-year profit forecast intact. The Stamford, Connecticut-based company, which sells Marlboro cigarettes outside the US, has been working to grow revenue from smoke-free alternatives as consumers in some markets increasingly move away from traditional cigarettes. Philip Morris continues to expect full-year adjusted earnings per share of $8.11 to $8.26, excluding currency effects. Quarterly revenue rose 5.5% to $11.44 billion, compared with analysts' estimate of $11.28 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company reported adjusted profit of $2.36 per share for the quarter, compared with analysts' average estimate of $2.29 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: Poland says social media firms are 'silent ally' of Russia, threatens fines
item.description: Social media platforms are a "silent ally" of Russia in a "digital war" and are doing nothing to curb disinformation, Polish Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on Wednesday, threatening fines for firms that ignore state requests.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Social media platforms are a "silent ally" of Russia in a "digital war" and are doing nothing to curb disinformation, Polish Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on Wednesday, threatening fines for firms that ignore state requests. Poland and other Western countries have on many occasions accused Russia of [USN:L8N43U235 TEXT:"spreading disinformation to sow division and destabilise their societies"]. Moscow denies such accusations and says Western leaders are intentionally exaggerating the threat from Russia for their own political ends. Data from Poland's NASK National Research Institute showed platforms acted on fewer than a quarter of the more than 65,000 reports of fake accounts and disinformation it sent them in the first half of 2026. Discord, Google, Meta, X, Telegram and TikTok did not immediately respond to requests for comment. "A digital war with Russia is underway, and within this digital war lies a front of disinformation. On this disinformation front, there is a silent ally to the Russian bots and the Kremlin’s GRU: social media platforms," Gawkowski said. "Social media platforms are doing nothing about this," he added during a press conference. Poland's NASK data showed that, of all cases of disinformation and fake accounts reported, social media platforms deleted 7% and moderated over 17%. "The data points not merely to a failure, but to deliberate action by the platforms — which profit from disinformation, use it, and treat it as a source of their revenue," Gawkowski said. He added that he issued a demand to the platforms to establish effective Polish-speaking content moderation teams, which would maintain a direct, real-time link to the relevant entities reporting such content. He also demanded the elimination of what he called sham appeals processes, the immediate removal of any identified bot networks and a reduction in response times for all such reports. "Furthermore, I have made it clear that any state request left unfulfilled by these platforms will trigger proceedings to impose financial penalties upon them," Gawkowski also said.

item.title: Heineken ordered to pay €111 million in damages, interest to Greek rival
item.description: Dutch beer company Heineken on Wednesday said a Dutch court had awarded Macedonian Thrace Brewery €111 million ($125 million) in damages and interest in a case it brought against Heineken's Greek subsidiary Athenian Brewery.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dutch beer company Heineken (HEIN.AS) on Wednesday said a Dutch court had awarded Macedonian Thrace Brewery €111 million ($125 million) in damages and interest in a case it brought against Heineken's Greek subsidiary Athenian Brewery. Heineken said it disagreed with the reasoning of the court and would appeal the decision, which related to conduct by Athenian Brewery in the Greek beer market between 1998 and 2014. In 2015, the Greek competition watchdog had already fined Athenian Brewery €31.5 million for abuse of its dominant position in the production and distribution of beer. In a follow-up case, the Dutch court now awarded MTB €43 million in damages and €68 million in accrued interest. Heineken said that the damages claim made by MTB had not been realistic, and said the court had made assumptions about MTB's sales, pricing and profitability in a hypothetical scenario. "Those assumptions should be carefully tested against the available economic evidence and market developments during the relevant period," the brewer said. "We do not believe the damages awarded adequately reflect those considerations." ($1 = 0.8910 euros)

item.title: How cheap Chinese antibiotics threaten Europe's last major penicillin plant
item.description: Tucked away in the green foothills of the Austrian Alps, the last fully integrated European penicillin plant faces an uncertain future in the shadow of rising Chinese industrial power.
item.dc:creator: Marleen Kaesebier, Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: Tucked away in the green foothills of the Austrian Alps, the last fully integrated European penicillin plant faces an uncertain future in the shadow of rising Chinese industrial power. The reason: China is churning out the same antibiotics and ingredients as the Sandoz factory in Kundl, Austria, at much lower cost for the European market. The falling prices are a boon for cost-conscious European governments' public healthcare programs but an existential threat to the Kundl site - the only one making penicillin from start to finish in Europe, including key active ingredients. After a number of peers announced they were closing or moving production to China, the plant has become a focal point for a widening debate about the West's self-sufficiency. And, just three years after a €200-million ($225-million) expansion that included €50 million of public funds, Sandoz has asked the European Commission to open an anti-dumping investigation that could result in tariff measures against Beijing. If the plant went out of business, Europe "would be fully dependent" on China, Kundl site manager Stephanie Jedner told Reuters in offices looking out over the plant's gleaming storage tanks, ringed by the Tyrolean Alps. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin a century ago in London, and it remains the main antibiotic class for life-threatening infections. Today, the manufacturing of ingredients for some 1.5 billion daily doses Europe administers each year is dominated by China. China's share of EU imports of penicillins and their derivatives in mostly bulk active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) form has nearly doubled from 44% in 2019 to 86% last year, Eurostat data show, coinciding with Beijing's "Made in China" 10-year plan to move up the global manufacturing value chain. Meanwhile, Europe's exports of the same are today barely a fifth of their early 2000s peak. It's one example of how China has graduated from textiles and assembly plants to advanced manufacturing and traditionally European industries from pharmaceuticals to machine tools. With the EU goods trade deficit with China ballooning to around €1 billion per day in 2025, double the level of 2020, [USN:L6N46017V TEXT:"policymakers are scrambling"] for new measures to protect companies and jobs. Sandoz, in written evidence to British lawmakers earlier this year, said Kundl's capacity to supply Europe was "not commercially sustainable" unless governments paid more for penicillin. It argued that Beijing's control of the penicillin supply chain creates an "inherent strategic risk" akin to China's stranglehold on critical minerals. "Antibiotic supply could feasibly become a tool of economic coercion or hybrid warfare, particularly during periods of diplomatic tension," Sandoz wrote in the submission to lawmakers, asking for more support. MEDICINE AS LEVERAGE IN TRADE WARS China spent years establishing itself as a reliable supplier of essential medicines and is increasingly a player in cutting-edge pharmaceuticals. Sandoz says up to 90% of global antibiotic active ingredients are now produced outside Europe, mainly in China, or in India with Chinese chemicals. "This is something that you should worry about," because China's market power gives it leverage to defend strategic interests, said Tim Rühlig, a China analyst at EU foreign policy think tank, the European Union Institute for Security Studies. China could face reputational damage if it used such leverage. Unlike its near monopoly over rare-earth refining, Chinese policy does not frame power in the antibiotic market in national-security terms. Nonetheless, Chinese economist Daokui Li, a former member of the Chinese central bank's monetary policy committee, spooked Western nations during the COVID-19 pandemic when he suggested supplies of APIs should be on the table in trade disputes. One US official in China, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters that Chinese counterparts had suggested in meetings that Beijing could cut off exports of APIs for some medicines as retaliation in a trade conflict. The Chinese foreign ministry said economic and trade differences with the EU could be resolved through dialogue and consultation. "China consistently opposes all forms of trade protectionism," it said in response to Reuters questions. The US State Department did not immediately provide comment. For European policymakers, the withering of such a strategic industry leaves the bloc vulnerable to restrictions on supplies during pandemics or conflicts, said Bostjan Ceh, head of business development at Labena, Slovenia-based pharmaceutical contract research and development firm. "It would seriously compromise Europe's ability to cope with a health crisis," Ceh said. Only after the COVID-19 pandemic – when Europe noticed its dependence on Asian medical supplies – did policymakers begin treating pharmaceutical output as a strategic matter, said Anna Mihaylova, a policy expert at the Medical University of Plovdiv. Alarm bells sounded in 2022, when supplies of amoxicillin, the penicillin type made at Kundl, ran low in Europe during a surge in respiratory infections after the pandemic. A year later, citing repeated shortages, the European Commission approved €28.3 million toward the Kundl expansion, which raised production capacity by 20%. SHIFTING DEPENDENCIES Wearing a white coat and safety goggles, Cecile Stolz, head of Sandoz's manufacturing unit in Kundl, demonstrated in a small vial how green mould is cultivated to make the compound Scottish scientist Fleming in 1928 found destroyed harmful bacteria. Fleming's discovery won him a Nobel prize. For years after, China depended heavily on Europe for production of penicillin and other generic drugs. But Beijing's industrial investment has now reversed the roles, said analyst Rühlig. China's newfound dominance also stems from fewer environmental regulations, drastically lower labour costs and state subsidies, along with investment by Western pharmaceutical companies seeking cost savings. At the Sandoz site, which employs more than 2,000 people, Stolz's team ferments nutrients in metal vats to produce the penicillin. The process is energy intensive, another factor making Europe's producers less competitive: EU electricity prices for energy-intensive industries averaged nearly 50% above China in 2025, International Energy Agency statistics show. Europe's high energy costs are acutely felt at the Kundl plant, which uses as much energy as the nearby city of Innsbruck, home to over 130,000 people, said its manager Jedner at the site Sandoz shares with former parent Novartis (NOVN.S) and chemicals maker BASF < BASFn.DE >. As energy prices rise, Europe's penicillin prices have been flat or falling, she added. CHEAP ANTIBIOTICS, BUT AT WHAT COST? Sandoz complains it cannot raise prices due to competition and the procurement processes of European countries. The Kundl plant remains vulnerable, the company says, because of European governments' policy of procuring medicine based on the lowest price rather than seeking to maintain diverse supplies. The company argues China is flooding the market with cheap APIs. In March, it filed a complaint to the European Commission about China's hold on parts of the antibiotics market. The case centres on proving Chinese amoxicillin APIs are being sold in Europe below production cost, propped up by subsidies. The European Commission is expected to open the anti-dumping probe soon, though the timing remains unclear due to a backlog of complaints, EU trade experts, European officials and China scholars told Reuters. The people told Reuters EU duties were likely to be levied given Europe is hardening its approach to China more broadly. Of 23 ongoing EU anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations, all but three have China as the sole or joint target. The Commission declined to comment. Other outcomes are possible. European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic recently announced a deal with Beijing to lower its exports of hybrid vehicles rather than imposing tariffs, a bid to salvage Europe's automakers. In public statements, Beijing says its subsidy support is in line with WTO rules. It accuses other countries of protectionism hurting global supply chains. As Sandoz struggles with global trade dynamics, its CEO Richard Saynor said that to be sustainable, the life-saving medicines need more pricing power than everyday candy. "I find it upsetting that we sell a pack of antibiotics more cheaply than a packet of Ricola in Switzerland or a Mars Bar in the UK," he told Reuters. "We take a lot of these things for granted – and we take them for granted until they're no longer around."

item.title: Ministerien wollen Pflicht-Elementarschutz für alle Wohnhäuser
item.description: In Deutschland sollen künftig nach den Vorstellungen des Justiz- und des Finanzministeriums alle Wohnhäuser zumindest teilweise gegen die Folgen von Überschwemmungen, Starkregen, Erdrutschen und ähnlichen Naturgefahren versichert werden. Die beiden Ministerien legten am Mittwoch ein Diskussionspapier für einen besseren Schutz gegen Elementarschäden vor, das als Grundlage für Gespräche mit den Bundesländern und den Versichererverbänden dienen soll. Danach sollen neue Wohngebäudeversicherungen künftig standardmäßig einen Elementarschutz mit maximal 20.000 Euro Selbstbehalt enthalten. Bei bestehenden Policen soll der Elementarschutz nach einem Jahr automatisch einbezogen werden, wenn der Versicherungsnehmer nicht widerspricht.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In Deutschland sollen künftig nach den Vorstellungen des Justiz- und des Finanzministeriums alle Wohnhäuser zumindest teilweise gegen die Folgen von Überschwemmungen, Starkregen, Erdrutschen und ähnlichen Naturgefahren versichert werden. Die beiden Ministerien legten am Mittwoch ein Diskussionspapier für einen besseren Schutz gegen Elementarschäden vor, das als Grundlage für Gespräche mit den Bundesländern und den Versichererverbänden dienen soll. Danach sollen neue Wohngebäudeversicherungen künftig standardmäßig einen Elementarschutz mit maximal 20.000 Euro Selbstbehalt enthalten. Bei bestehenden Policen soll der Elementarschutz nach einem Jahr automatisch einbezogen werden, wenn der Versicherungsnehmer nicht widerspricht. Ganz ohne einen Elementar-Versicherungsschutz sollen Haus- und Wohnungseigentümer aber nach dem Willen der SPD-geführten Ministerien in keinem Fall bleiben. Geprüft werden soll allenfalls, ob sie alternativ eine billigere Mindestversicherung abschließen können, bei der sie im Ernstfall aber auf den ersten 100.000 Euro Schaden sitzenbleiben. Das könnte vor allem für Eigentümer attraktiv sein, deren Häuser in hochwassergefährdeten Gebieten liegen und deren Versicherungsprämien deshalb besonders hoch ausfielen. Immerhin 0,4 Prozent aller Wohnhäuser stehen an Orten, wo einmal in zehn Jahren Hochwasser zu erwarten ist. In diesem Fall müssten sie aber akzeptieren, dass ihnen der Staat nicht finanziell unter die Arme greift. Zwar sind 98 Prozent aller Wohngebäude in Deutschland gegen Feuer, Sturm oder Hagel versichert, aber nur 59 Prozent auch gegen Ereignisse wie Überschwemmungen oder Erdrutsche, die im Klimawandel häufiger auftreten dürften als bisher. Im Schnitt verursachen sie in Deutschland nach Angaben des Versicherer-Verbandes GDV Schäden von rund zwei Milliarden Euro pro Jahr. Bei solchen Katastrophen springt meist der Staat mit Steuergeld ein, um teilweise existenzbedrohende Schäden abzumildern. Das zu ändern, hatte sich die schwarze-rote Bundesregierung bereits im Koalitionsvertrag auf die Fahnen geschrieben. Wie das geschehen soll, ist aber umstritten. Nach 25 Jahren Diskussion liege nun dafür ein Vorschlag auf dem Tisch, erklärte Justiz- und Verbraucherschutzministerin Stefanie Hubig. "Unser Vorschlag bietet die Chance, beim besseren Versicherungsschutz vor Flut und Starkregen endlich voranzukommen." Es gelte aber, viele unterschiedliche Interessen unter einen Hut zu bringen. Zudem müsse der Schutz bezahlbar bleiben - für Eigentümer und für Mieter. Diskutiert werden solle unter anderem, ob Eigentümer die Kosten für den erweiterten Schutz über die Nebenkosten auf die Mieter abwälzen dürfen oder nicht. Die Länder und Verbände haben bis zum 2. Dezember Zeit, sich zu den Vorschlägen zu äußern. Erst danach soll ein Gesetzentwurf ausgearbeitet werden. Der Gesamtverband der Deutschen Versicherungswirtschaft (GDV) sieht eine Versicherungspflicht bisher kritisch und pocht flankierend auf mehr Prävention. Bauverbote etwa in Überschwemmungsgebieten sind in dem Vorschlag der Ministerien ebenso angesprochen wie die staatliche Förderung von Schutzmaßnahmen für gefährdete Häuser.

item.title: Water rationing, rubbish pile-up raise disease fears in Yemen's besieged Taiz
item.description: Fighting between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-allied Houthi group since September has cut key supply routes, worsening shortages of water, food and fuel in and around the city.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: Families have started rationing water in and around [USN:L8N46125M TEXT:"Yemen's Taiz city"], where renewed fighting has disrupted fuel supplies and access to water systems serving 3 million people, aid groups and UN agencies said. Meanwhile, mounting piles of rubbish along major roads are raising fears of disease outbreaks in the city, Yemen's third-largest. Fighting between the Saudi-backed government and the Iran-allied Houthi group since September has cut key supply routes, including the Taiz-Aden corridor, worsening [USN:L6N4620L1 TEXT:"shortages of water, food and fuel"] in and around the city. The lack of fuel is hampering the operation of water pumps and hospitals, while disruption to waste collection has left rubbish piled along roads of the city, a stronghold of anti-Houthi forces which is now under siege by the armed movement. The Taiz governorate hosts nearly half of the 250,000 people displaced by the latest escalation, aid groups said. "The state of the rubbish in the city is very wretched, and the build-up is terrible, like nothing before,” Taiz resident Abdelbari al-Qadi told Reuters. Sanitation worker Ali Ahmed said authorities could no longer go to the main dumping site because of clashes, and they were forced to burn it in the streets. 'EXTREMELY DANGEROUS SITUATION' FOR CHILDREN, SAYS RELIEF OFFICIAL Families are rationing drinking water as diesel shortages hobble pumping stations and sanitation systems, said Akhil Iyer, UNICEF's representative in Yemen. "I get the water with difficulty. We wait in queues from the morning until our turn comes,” Alaa Khalil told Reuters while people queued to fill jerry cans in Taiz, where most residents depend on trucked water. Access to the Al-Dhubab aquifer, a major source of trucked water for Taiz, has been restricted, while fuel disruptions have affected pumps, creating a severe water crisis, said Wathiq Aghbari, director general of the Local Water and Sanitation Authority in the governorate. Water production in Taiz has fallen by about 50%, according to Save the Children. “We find children in an extremely dangerous situation where they are not able to have their basic needs satisfied. They are not able to access sufficient food and water and healthcare,” said Rishana Haniffa, Save the Children's country director for Yemen. Aid groups are exploring other sources, including a shallow aquifer west of the city. The cost of a water truck has tripled from about 23,000 Yemeni rials ($14.80) before the latest escalation to about 70,000 rials ($45), according to UNICEF. CARE International says cash assistance is buying less food and water as prices rise. “We feel the situation is really getting out of hand unless we able to negotiate access to have water tankers come in to the city,” said Iman Abdullahi, CARE Yemen country director. RUBBISH BUILD-UP 'WILL CAUSE DISEASES', SAYS HEALTH OFFICIAL "The build-up of rubbish is very harmful and will cause diseases, whether respiratory or otherwise," said Abdulrahman al-Sabri, director of Taiz Governorate's Health Office, adding that dengue fever and cholera cases were spreading. Cholera cases have tripled since early September from 221 to 683 this month, while hospitals face medicine shortages and 12 facilities have fuel supplies sufficient for only about four days, the World Health Organization said. A doctor who asked not to be named for security reasons said some families could not reach healthcare facilities because of fighting around the city. The Danish Refugee Council said the impact of deteriorating water and sanitation conditions could spread beyond Taiz city. It pointed to overstretched resources in crowded displacement sites across the governorates of Taiz, Lahj, Abyan and Aden. The spread of disease could also worsen hunger in Taiz governorate, UNICEF said. It has identified 52,000 acutely malnourished children in Taiz so far this year. Road closures have halted UNICEF's deliveries of a therapeutic food for severely malnourished children in Taiz.

item.title: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord, Ankara says
item.description: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said. In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the "Badr Memorandum of Understanding" in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships. "The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development. "By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defense industrial capacities, and enable the fulfillment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added. Turkey, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war. In August, it signed a [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"mutual defence pact"] with nuclear-armed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"attack on all"]. Ankara also has [USN:L4N3TQ07F TEXT:"close ties"] with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry. The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives.

item.title: TAUX Le rendement de l'OAT à 10 ans atteint 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002 (actualisé)
item.description: Le rendement de l'obligation souveraine française à 10 ans a atteint mercredi le seuil psychologique de 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002, un nouveau signe de l'inquiétude des investisseurs quant à la capacité de la deuxième économie de la zone euro à réduire son déficit.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Le rendement de l'obligation souveraine française à 10 ans a atteint mercredi le seuil psychologique de 5% pour la première fois depuis juillet 2002, un nouveau signe de l'inquiétude des investisseurs quant à la capacité de la deuxième économie de la zone euro à réduire son déficit. Le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans prend 7 points de base (pdb) pour s'établir à 4,9877% à 12h00 GMT, après avoir brièvement dépassé les 5% plus tôt en séance. Les craintes concernant le budget de la France pour 2027, en plein examen parlementaire, ainsi que la polarisation des débats politiques à la suite des violences en marge des mobilisations du week-end dernier, ont de nouveau mis à rude épreuve le marché obligataire, déjà sous pression en raison de la flambée de l'inflation liée à la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Bien que les tensions sur le marché obligataire soient généralisées, elles sont particulièrement intenses dans les pays les plus endettés, comme la France ou l'Italie ; le rendement des obligations de cette dernière prend plus de six pdb mercredi, pour s'établir à 4,5874%. En Allemagne, dont l'obligation à 10 ans sert de référence pour la zone euro, le rendement du Bund n'avance que de 2 pdb, à 3,4143% Le "spread", c'est-à-dire l'écart de rendement entre les obligations d'État allemandes et françaises, a de nouveau frôlé mercredi les 160 pdb, évoluant à des niveaux qui n'ont plus été observés depuis fin 2011. Il ressort à 157 en début d'après-midi. Le "spread" est un indicateur de la prime de risque exigée par les investisseurs pour détenir des titres de dette français par rapport à ceux de Berlin, considérés comme plus sûrs. "Remettre les finances publiques en ordre passerait notamment par l'adoption d'un budget cet automne qui irait dans le sens d'une réduction du déficit. Mais les finances publiques sont avant tout un enjeu de long terme et le résultat de l'élection présidentielle sera à ce titre déterminant", écrit dans une note Sylvain Bersinger, économiste et fondateur du cabinet Bersingéco. L'approche de l'élection présidentielle de 2027 constitue ainsi un facteur d'incertitude qui exacerbe encore davantage les tensions, d'autant plus que les options les plus extrêmes sont en tête dans les sondages. "On comprend, à la vue des sondages, la frilosité des investisseurs envers la dette française", dit-il. La hausse des rendements obligataires a des répercussions sur l'ensemble de l'économie, rendant les emprunts plus coûteux, y compris le crédit immobilier. "Le seuil des 4% n'a été dépassé que fin juillet, faisant du troisième trimestre, celui de la plus forte hausse des taux d'emprunt d'Etat français en près de 40 ans", souligne Julie Bachet, directrice générale de Vousfinancer, un réseau de 150 agences de courtage en crédit immobilier. "Les taux moyens sur 20 ans sont autour de 3,7%, soit plus d'un point sous l'OAT. Les banques rognent donc sur leurs marges pour continuer à prêter. Cette situation ne peut pas durer indéfiniment et les barèmes vont continuer à augmenter dans les prochaines semaines, plus rapidement que nous ne l'avions prévu", souligne-t-elle.

item.title: GSK is two shots away from clean bill of health
item.description: One of Europe’s most cheaply valued drugmakers, the £75 bln group run by Luke Miels is turning a corner. Fears over expiring patents are easing thanks to a booming oncology unit. A £40 bln sales target looks hard, but Miels may fix that with canny dealmaking and luck in the lab.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Donnellan
item.content:encoded: If GSK (GSK.L) were a patient doctors would be starting to hope that it’s on the mend. Despite being one of the cheapest of the global pharma stocks, new CEO Luke Miels is ploughing money into research and development and doing savvy deals. The big question is can he deliver on his target of over £40 billion in sales by 2031 . Signs of a recovery have appeared slowly. When Miels’ predecessor Emma Walmsley was in charge, she spun out the consumer goods business which makes Sensodyne toothpaste, now called Haleon (HLN.L) . Investors hoped the surgery would unleash a leaner, less indebted business that could focus its efforts on dealmaking and its core areas of vaccines, HIV and general medicines including inhalers and antibiotics. So far, that's yet to translate into a material valuation bump: GSK trades at around 10 times forward earnings, in line with its multiple when Haleon was spun off in 2022 , and below peers like AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , Novartis (NOVN.S) and Roche (ROPC.S) . The main reason is fear of what comes next. Dolutegravir, GSK’s star HIV treatment which accounted for 17% of GSK’s near £33 billion of sales last year, loses patent protection in the US from 2028. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha expect revenue in that division to half by 2031. Vaccines have also lost steam. Anti vaccine sentiment is growing in the US, and analysts expect the division to grow sales by an average of less than 2% over the next five years. However, Miels is plugging these holes partly by bolstering the group’s growing cancer business. Last year, sales in oncology rose by over 40% to nearly £2 billion and they are expected to reach over £5 billion pounds by 2031. And he’s hoping to boost that further through deals and in-house drug development. In June, he splurged [USN:L6N42H0KM TEXT:"$11 billion"] on US lung cancer specialist Nuvalent. The business won regulatory approval for one of its drugs a month after the deal was announced and GSK is expecting to hear about another remedy later this year. This week GSK won regulatory backing for a new rectal cancer drug. Growth in GSK’s oncology business should help offset the decline in HIV as dolutegravir's patents expire. The cancer success isn't the only sign that GSK's plan to boost in-house drug development is paying off. Miels is expecting to start over 20 new late stage drug trials this year. Potential blockbuster drugs include a hepatitis B remedy bepirovirsen which it reckons will generate £2 billion in annual sales. Berenberg analysts estimate the group's likely return on research investment is now over 10%, healthily exceeding the sector's 8% cost of capital. GSK is still some way off hitting Miels' target to reach £40 billion of sales by 2031. But the gap is closing: Analysts polled by Visible Alpha estimate sales of £37 billion that year, up from less than £34 billion a year ago. To hit the magic number, Miels will probably need to do more small deals, as well as keep securing fresh drug approvals. But the danger that he will resort to more large risky takeovers is probably easing. That, along with GSK's broader turnaround, means its valuation should start to catch up with its healthier peers. Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn . GSK will unveil its third quarter earnings on October 28. The US Food and Drug Administration on October 19 approved GSK’s Jemperli, an immunotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: US Democratic congressional nominee Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank
item.description: Brad Lander, an ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani who is running for the US Congress next month, was among 90 individuals detained by Israeli authorities in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, according to Rabbis for Human rights, an Israeli rights group.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brad Lander, an ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani who is running for the US Congress next month, was among 90 individuals detained by Israeli authorities in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, according to Rabbis for Human rights, an Israeli rights group. item.title: Husqvarna looks east as Chinese rivals chip away at robot lawnmower lead
item.description: Husqvarna has moved some production of robotic lawnmowers from Britain to the Czech Republic and is weighing increased manufacturing in Asia, its CEO said on Wednesday, as cheaper rivals chip away at its lead in the market it pioneered three decades ago.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Calero
item.content:encoded: Husqvarna (HUSQb.ST) has moved some production of robotic lawnmowers from Britain to the Czech Republic and is weighing increased manufacturing in Asia, its CEO said on Wednesday, as cheaper rivals chip away at its lead in the market it pioneered three decades ago. Drought across much of Europe left less grass to mow during the third quarter, hurting sales at a time when consumers were already holding back on garden equipment purchases. But the problems go beyond the weather. "We have lost some volume this year," CEO Glen Instone told Reuters, saying Husqvarna had lost more European market share in units sold than in sales value. The Swedish company has held its ground among traditional dealers, but faces much tougher competition in shops and online, sales channels in which it has historically been less active. That is forcing it to reconsider how much it can cut prices without undermining the premium positioning that has long distinguished its products. Instone said Husqvarna would likely have to lower the roughly €1,000 ($1,122) starting price of its Husqvarna-branded robotic mowers, though he ruled out competing with machines costing less than €500. The challenge extends to how and where Husqvarna makes its machines. Instone said the company had moved some robotic mower production from Newton Aycliffe in Britain to Czechia to cut costs. The transfer was completed this autumn and affected around 50 roles in the British plant, a company spokesperson said. Instone said Husqvarna was also considering production in Asia, although longer shipping times and the need to hold more stock could eat into potential savings from such a move. The company said earlier on Wednesday it was moving production of some battery-powered handheld tools from two European factories to Asia, including its own plant in China and external suppliers, with the move to be fully effective in 2028. It did not specify how many jobs would be affected. Just last year, Husqvarna had begun moving production from China to Europe to reduce its exposure to US tariffs. Its Czech subsidiary also initiated an EU investigation into alleged dumping of Chinese robotic mowers last year, although Instone said Husqvarna could compete without additional duties. Despite 935 million Swedish crowns ($94.4 million) of realised savings this year, weak sales and rising costs have continued to erode Husqvarna's earnings. But Instone said further savings could restore profitability in 2027 even without European demand recovery. The company's shares plunged around 10% to a 14-year low in Stockholm after a bigger-than-expected [USN:L8N467068 TEXT:"quarterly loss"]. ($1 = €0.8910) ($1 = 9.9050 Swedish crowns)

item.title: South Korea's Korai Flix to go public in US via $3.5 billion SPAC deal
item.description: South Korean entertainment platform Korai Flix will go public in the U.S. through a $3.5 billion merger with special purpose acquisition company APEX Tech Acquisition , the companies said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean entertainment platform Korai Flix will go public in the U.S. through a $3.5 billion merger with special purpose acquisition company APEX Tech Acquisition (APXBU.O) , the companies said on Wednesday. The deal comes as SPACs, an alternative route to public markets, are [USN:L4N44P1H0 TEXT:"making a comeback"] in the US after years of subdued activity. Korai's platform, launched in 2024, offers AI-generated short dramas and AI companion avatars to roughly 26 million users across 15 countries in Asia. Users can also use tools to create such content in various visual styles. Microdramas, short episodic vertical videos delivered in two-minute episodes for viewing on phones, [USN:L6N44B0T8 TEXT:"have surged in popularity"] worldwide. The format is cheap to produce and can be generated rapidly using artificial intelligence. In the first half of 2026, microdramas on YouTube garnered more than 6.5 billion views, while watch time grew over 50% from a year earlier. Korean entertainment content is also flourishing across the world following the success of K-pop, K-dramas and other Korean cultural exports. Korai will be the latest South Korea-linked entertainment platform to go public in US. Naver-backed Webtoon Entertainment (WBTN.O) , which owns novel distribution platform Wattpad, [USN:L4N3IP1AL TEXT:"debuted in New York in 2024"] through a traditional IPO. A SPAC is a shell company that raises capital through an initial public offering and then uses the funds to merge with or acquire a private company, taking it public without a traditional IPO. The SPAC deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The combined company will be renamed Krflix Group and is expected to list on the New York Stock Exchange.

item.title: AT&T raises annual profit forecast on strong demand for bundled plans
item.description: AT&T raised its annual adjusted profit forecast on Wednesday after beating quarterly revenue and profit estimates, betting on its service bundles to drive growth and keep customers from switching to rivals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AT&T (T.N) raised its annual adjusted profit forecast on Wednesday after beating quarterly revenue and profit estimates, betting on its service bundles to drive growth and keep customers from switching to rivals. About 43% of households signing up for AT&T's internet services also opt for its wireless plans, helping the company build stickier customer relationships and reduce disconnects as competition intensifies in the US telecom market. AT&T added 379,000 net monthly bill-paying wireless subscribers during the third quarter, compared with 379,300 additions estimated by FactSet The company also reported a $2.6 billion non-cash impairment charge related to the [USN:L6N45Z18X TEXT:"planned sale"] of its Mexico wireless business for $2 billion It now expects annual adjusted profit per share of about $2.40, compared with its prior forecast of $2.25 to $2.35 US carriers are looking beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions to bundled services and customer loyalty programs to attract and retain subscribers AT&T has been doubling down on fiber expansion, striking a [USN:L4N45L15B TEXT:"multi-year deal"] worth more than $3 billion with Corning last month for fiber and cable supplies It also acquired Lumen's [USN:L6N3RT0UJ TEXT:"fiber business"] in May 2025 for $5.75 billion to expand its broadband footprint and meet rising demand for high-speed connectivity This has helped AT&T secure record broadband additions, with 442,000 new fiber internet users and 327,000 new fixed wireless subscribers added in the third quarter Revenue for the quarter rose 5.3% from a year earlier to $32.3 billion, beating analysts' estimates of $31.69 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG Adjusted profit per share for the quarter came in at 65 cents, above estimates of 60 cents Shares of the company fell 3.8% in volatile premarket trading

item.title: Nasdaq futures lead gains as SpaceX, Super Micro results lift AI stocks
item.description: Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday as quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer revived the AI trade, while Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress investors.
item.dc:creator: Purvi Agarwal, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq led gains on Wednesday as quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer revived the AI trade, while Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress investors. Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm (SPCX.O) rose 7.2% in premarket trading after he said on Tuesday that [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX"] and Tesla (TSLA.O) would be "a good idea". SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. Tesla shares were up 1.4%. "There is potential for substantial gains in its AI business, as AI infrastructure is capital intensive, and SpaceX has more means than many smaller companies ... if AI stress mounts, SpaceX could swallow up infrastructure business from smaller competitors," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote. Ozkardeskaya said that a merger with Tesla could be a good idea if "the two companies can prove that the synergies create value for both of them", but could be rejected by investors if Tesla was "better off exploring AI synergies with other companies". Other space stocks were also higher, with Rocket Lab (RKLB.O) , Planet Labs (PL.N) and Intuitive Machines (LUNR.O) adding between 2.6% and 3.9%. EchoStar (ECHO.O) , which holds SpaceX shares, rose 4.3%. Super Micro (SMCI.O) jumped 10.9% after the AI server maker [USN:L4N4661QH TEXT:"forecast"] quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. Peers HPE (HPE.N) and Dell (DELL.N) rose 4.5% and 5.5% respectively. Investors drew comfort from the reports as concerns over the profitability of the AI buildout triggered a selloff in AI-linked stocks last week, with data center operator CoreWeave (CRWV.O) at the center of the storm. It was up 2.5% before the bell on Wednesday. Most chipmakers also rose, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) up 2.1%, Intel (INTC.O) gaining 2.3% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) adding 1.9%. Semiconductors have had a volatile month so far, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) marking eight consecutive sessions of declines, its longest losing streak in 18 years. Despite a brief reprieve on Monday, the index is trading at two-month lows. The Dow outshone the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq on Tuesday on the back of robust gains in healthcare stocks. On the other hand, Netflix (NFLX.O) dropped over 6.6% after the streaming giant issued [USN:L6N4661BU TEXT:"a weaker-than-expected forecast"] for its fourth-quarter profit, days after laying off 6% of its workforce. Results from Meta (META.O) and Tesla will be parsed after markets close. At 7:34 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 64 points, or 0.12%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 20.75 points, or 0.27%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 196.75 points, or 0.67%. Before the bell, AT&T (T.N) fell 3.5% despite beating [USN:L4N4670UN TEXT:"third-quarter"] revenue and profit estimates. Elevance Health (ELV.N) rose around 1% after the [USN:L4N4670SF TEXT:"health insurer"] lifted its 2026 profit forecast. Meanwhile, oil prices remained elevated, with Brent crude futures trading near $110 a barrel. Data last week confirmed that price pressures were seeping into the US economy, and had broadened out beyond energy products, supporting the case for another interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. The central bank meets next week.

item.title: France's Macron vows no repeat of riots as Yellow Vests mobilise
item.description: The Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a major Paris march on Saturday that will present the government with its next big test.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to prevent a repeat of [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"last weekend's"] riots and looting, as the Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a major Paris march on Saturday that will present the government with its next big test. Macron said on Wednesday that those seeking to cause disorder at the next protests would be stopped, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met union leaders in an effort to defuse one of the worst crises France has faced in recent years. A representative of the "Gilets Jaunes" (Yellow Vests) movement, a grassroots group not tied to the unions, presented plans for a march across the heart of Paris, including areas that were ransacked just days ago. Student groups have also called for protests the same day to push demands for greater investment in education. Yellow Vest activists are seeking to revive their campaign, which emerged in 2018, against rising living costs and declining public services. INVESTORS FRET, FRENCH BORROWING COSTS CLIMB Last weekend's demonstrations rapidly degenerated into rampant violence, especially in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], which the overwhelmed police took hours to contain. Highlighting investor concern over the situation, French government borrowing costs have jumped this week, pushing benchmark 10-year bond yields to 5%, [USN:L8N4670MT TEXT:"their highest level"] since July 2002. Analysts said the move reflected worries that the unrest could complicate government efforts to repair strained public finances at a time of already mounting budget pressures. Macron said he would meet intelligence officials, Lecornu and other ministers on Thursday to obtain a detailed account of the October 17 unrest. "Those who want to cause disorder in city centres next Saturday will be prevented from doing so," Macron told reporters during a visit to Qatar, where he has been seeking energy deals as France grapples with rising fuel costs. "There must be no wavering at the top of the state." MACRON SAYS TRUMP SPREADING MISLEADING INFORMATION Government ministers have promised a vastly reinforced security operation after acknowledging shortcomings in their initial response, with troops expected to be deployed alongside additional police. Macron accused some foreign leaders of spreading misinformation about what had happened. US President Donald Trump in particular [USN:L1N46602Q TEXT:"has blamed"] the turbulence on mass migration and radical Islam, saying it was a warning for Americans. Asked whether he was referring to Trump, Macron said: "Among others", adding that some foreign politicians were looking to make political capital at the expense of France. "We don’t need that. We already have difficulties to deal with," he said. 'LEGITIMATE ANGER' In a letter to unions ahead of Wednesday's meeting, Lecornu said their talks should focus on ensuring "the indispensable freedom to demonstrate", which he said some were trying to curtail by associating it with "unacceptable acts". France's main unions have separately called a nationwide mobilisation for November 5. "There is huge and legitimate anger, and the answer to that situation is not repression. It is a political response. That's what I will tell the prime minister today," Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, told RTL radio. After the meeting, Binet told reporters the government made no new announcements, but did say that youth organisations would be invited for talks. A second consecutive night of local curfews passed without major incidents in areas hit by the unrest, offering the government some respite as it prepared for fresh demonstrations. The unrest has triggered a political backlash ahead of presidential elections next year, with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls. "The government has lost control of everything," far-right leader Marine Le Pen told Franceinfo radio. The hard-left France Unbowed (LFI), which has denied allegations by ministers of fueling the unrest, criticised plans to deploy troops onto the streets of Paris. "Demonstrators are not enemies within. The French government must not go to war against its own people," LFI's parliamentary group said in a statement. Protests in other European countries, including [USN:L1N4650LE TEXT:"Italy"] and [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"Albania"], have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes. [USN:L8N4661X4 TEXT:"Italy approved"] a raft of security measures on Tuesday, including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration and tougher penalties for rioters in response to the turbulence last weekend.

item.title: Nvidia-Chef Huang sieht großes Robotik-Potenzial in Europa
item.description: Der US-Chipkonzern Nvidia vertraut auf die Wachstumsaussichten europäischer Firmen. "Im zurückliegenden Jahr haben wir nahezu zehn Milliarden Dollar investiert", sagte Konzernchef Jensen Huang am Mittwoch in seiner Rede zum Auftakt der Konferenz GTC in Berlin. "Allein in der letzten Woche haben wir Beteiligungen an 14 Startups verkündet. Insgesamt sind wir inzwischen mehr als 12.000 Partnerschaften eingegangen."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der US-Chipkonzern Nvidia (NVDA.O) vertraut auf die Wachstumsaussichten europäischer Firmen. "Im zurückliegenden Jahr haben wir nahezu zehn Milliarden Dollar investiert", sagte Konzernchef Jensen Huang am Mittwoch in seiner Rede zum Auftakt der Konferenz GTC in Berlin. "Allein in der letzten Woche haben wir Beteiligungen an 14 Startups verkündet. Insgesamt sind wir inzwischen mehr als 12.000 Partnerschaften eingegangen." Der kalifornische Halbleiterhersteller hält unter anderem Anteile an den deutschen Roboterbauern Agile Robots und Neura Robotics, dem KI-Entwickler Black Forest Labs sowie dem Satelliten-Hersteller Reflex Aerospace. Vor allem im Bereich humanoider Robotik habe Europa großes Potenzial, betonte Huang. "Keine Region hat sich so sehr der Herstellung von Mechatronik, Elektronik und mechanischen Systemen auf höchstem Niveau verschrieben wie Europa." Die dadurch gewonnenen Fertigkeiten und Daten bildeten eine hervorragende Grundlage für sogenannte Physische KI. Zur Demonstration holte der Nvidia-Chef mehrere "Microducks" auf die Bühne. Diese KI-gesteuerten zweibeinigen Roboter eines französischen Startups reagieren auf gesprochene Anweisungen. Sie setzen sich hin, schlagen Rad oder machen ein Nickerchen. VORKONFIGURIERTE SYSTEME FÜR ROBOTER UND ROBOTAXIS Um die Verbreitung humanoider Roboter zu beschleunigen, will Nvidia ein vorkonfiguriertes System anbieten. Entwickler müssten sich dann nicht erst mit der Abstimmung von Mechanik, Sensoren und Software herumschlagen, bevor sie die Maschinen für bestimmte Aufgaben trainieren, betonte Huang. Hierfür hat sein Unternehmen in Zusammenarbeit mit dem deutschen Startup Agile den "[USN:L6N4650VU TEXT:"Agile One SN"]" entwickelt. Der etwa 1,4 Meter große und 43 Kilogramm schwere zweibeinige Roboter ist vor allem für Forschungslabore gedacht. Huang stellte bei seiner Präsentation darüber hinaus "Hyperion" vor. Dabei handelt es sich um ein vorkonfiguriertes System aus Hard- und Software für autonome Fahrzeuge. Mithilfe dieser Technologie würden die Robotaxis unterschiedlicher Fahrdienst-Vermittler zu einer riesigen virtuellen Flotte vereinigt. Künftig würden auch Volkswagen, Volvo (VOLCARb.ST) und Mercedes (MBGn.DE) auf "Hyperion" setzen. Huangs Auftritt am Mittwoch wurde kurz durch Zwischenrufe unterbrochen. In der Übertragung der Veranstaltung waren ihre Forderungen nicht zu verstehen. Der Nvidia-Chef sicherte den Störern zu, er werde später mit ihnen sprechen. Sie wurden anschließend aus dem Saal geführt.

item.title: Turkey plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
item.description: Turkey will submit to parliament a mandate allowing for military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey will submit to parliament a mandate allowing for military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party told Reuters on Wednesday. The lawmaker, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the mandate would be sent to parliament once a bill ratifying the accord has been approved. Turkey [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"submitted"] the [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] — signed by the three countries in August — to parliament for ratification on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks. The AKP lawmaker said that no Turkish troops deployed to other countries under the pact would take part in offensive operations, adding that technical personnel and experts would be sent initially to help with air defences, electronic warfare technologies, and other defensive support. Earlier, two officials had told Reuters that [USN:L6N45T0WB TEXT:"Turkey's contribution"] was expected to be limited to military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far. Turkey, which has condemned the Houthi attacks, has also agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

item.title: Elevance lifts 2026 profit forecast on lower medical costs, higher premiums
item.description: Elevance Health on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results due to higher premiums and lower medical costs, driving the health insurer's shares 2.1% higher in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elevance Health (ELV.N) on Wednesday raised its annual profit forecast after posting better-than-expected quarterly results due to higher premiums and lower medical costs, driving the health insurer's shares 2.1% higher in premarket trading. Health insurers have been grappling with declining membership, as well as rising costs from elevated demand for behavioral health services and specialty drugs in government-backed plans. Elevance, like other health insurers, has adjusted its pricing to reflect higher medical costs. For the third quarter, the company said higher premium yields and service fees offset lower membership, helping the company's insurance business post a $1.1 billion rise in revenue from a year earlier. Last week, larger rival UnitedHealth Group (UNH.N) also raised its full-year profit forecast, attributing the improvement to plan design and new pricing on products. Elevance's upbeat quarterly performance reflects "stronger execution across our diversified portfolio and underscore the earnings power of the business," CEO Gail K. Boudreaux said. Medical membership of about 44.9 million as of September 30 decreased by 487,000 compared to the prior year, the company said. For the third quarter, the health insurer reported a medical loss ratio, the percentage of premiums spent on medical care, of 90.6%, lower than analysts' expectations of 91.17%. The company said lower costs were due to better performance in its Medicare Advantage plans for older Americans and those with disabilities as well as Obamacare plans compared to the prior year. The company also said it plans to deliver at least 12% growth in 2027 adjusted profit from an earnings baseline of at least $26.75 per share. Elevance forecast full-year adjusted profit to be at least $29 per share, compared with its previous outlook of at least $27 per share. Analysts on average estimate an annual profit of $27.23 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. On an adjusted basis, the company earned a profit of $6.99 per share, compared with analysts' average estimate of $4.68 per share.

item.title: How the Republican redistricting gambit faltered under Trump slump
item.description: Nine Republican-redrawn districts now lean Democratic or are too close to call.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: At President Donald Trump 's urging, Republicans pursued an unprecedented mid-decade redistricting campaign ahead of November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], redrawing dozens of US House of Representatives districts in an effort to preserve their narrow majority. With less than two weeks until Election Day, however, Trump's unpopularity has wiped out most of those gains, leaving Republicans scrambling to defend even districts they engineered to be safely conservative. As of June, Republicans had increased their advantage in 16 redrawn districts. Today, nine of those Republican-leaning districts are either expected to go to Democrats or are too close to call, according to a Reuters analysis of ratings from leading election forecasters. A 10th Republican district was thrown out by courts. Redistricting typically occurs only once a decade following the US Census' population count. But Texas Republicans tore up the state's existing US House map last summer with Trump's backing, setting off a multistate fight between the parties that Republicans [USN:L1N4250NA TEXT:"appeared to win"] handily. Democrats were only able to use redistricting to gain an edge in six districts. But what looked like a Republican victory has since been undercut by Trump's record-low approval rating, driven by the unpopular war in Iran and Americans' deep frustration with the resulting high gas prices. "It's a powerful lesson that you can be too smart for your own good when you try to predict the future," said Michael Li, a redistricting expert at New York University's Brennan Center for Justice. TEXAS, FLORIDA RACES NO LONGER SAFE BETS Most of the Republican gains were expected to come from Texas and Florida, where new maps reshaped nine Democratic-held seats into districts that Trump carried in 2024 by anywhere from 9 to 20 percentage points. But the collapse of Trump's support among Latino voters has upended the political calculus in those states. Analysts now view only one of those nine as a sure thing for Republicans, with six considered highly competitive. "I think the maps in Texas and Florida were way too confident that Hispanic voters would continue to vote for Republicans at the same level they did in 2024," said Erin Covey, who analyzes US House races for the Cook Political Report. "There is absolutely a world where Republicans don't flip any of the four seats they redrew in Florida." The median outcome for Republicans is a gain of around three seats from redistricting alone, Covey said. But if the Democratic wave turns into a tsunami, she added, Democrats could actually end up netting two seats through redistricting. That said, the national House map is objectively better for Republicans than it was prior to redistricting, according to Jacob Rubashkin, an analyst at Inside Elections. "The number of pickups is almost certain to fall well below expectation," he said. "It's also true that Republicans will still do better because they redistricted than had they lived and let live." Some of the newly redrawn districts are among the races that have drawn the most campaign spending, underscoring their competitiveness. Four of the six House races that have received the most outside spending from Republican-aligned groups - an average of more than $12 million each - are taking place in Republican-redistricted seats, according to campaign finance data. Democrats need to flip at least four House seats on November 3 to win control of the chamber. DEMOCRATS REACH DEEP INTO REPUBLICAN TERRITORY Even districts that once seemed unassailable are [USN:L6N45T19V TEXT:"potentially in reach"] for Democrats. After the US Supreme Court in April [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"hollowed out"] the Voting Rights Act's protections for districts with large minority populations, Alabama Republicans quickly dismantled one of the state's two predominantly Black districts in favor of a new, majority-white one that backed Trump by more than 14 percentage points in 2024. But now, two national forecasters, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia, both categorize the race as "Lean Republican," suggesting incumbent Democrat Shomari Figures could prevail in a strong Democratic wave. To be sure, Democrats may not carry every seat they redrew either. In California, where Democratic lawmakers passed a new map targeting five Republican-held seats, two Republicans are locked in tight contests with Democratic challengers, according to analysts. In some cases, the new maps could also have unintended consequences for incumbent Republicans. Under the updated Texas map, the seat of Republican Monica De La Cruz remained solidly Republican, with Trump winning the district's voters by nearly 18 percentage points. But most of that territory was new to her, forcing the incumbent to introduce herself to swaths of new voters. Her Democratic opponent, Bobby Pulido, is a well-known Tejano music star who has sought to transform his cultural popularity into political success. That seat is now widely seen as a tossup.

item.title: End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal
item.description: London-based Cai Baochun used to make a hefty profit reselling Hermes' famed Birkin bags for more than double their $10,000 retail price. Now he has stopped stockpiling them as second-hand prices fall.
item.dc:creator: Tassilo Hummel, Helen Reid, Alessandro Parodi
item.content:encoded: London-based Cai Baochun used to make a hefty profit reselling Hermes' (HRMS.PA) famed Birkin bags for more than double their $10,000 retail price. Now he has stopped stockpiling them as second-hand prices fall. “I don’t want to lose money,” said Cai, who started selling the bags on online platforms such as Vestiaire Collective and on social media in 2020 and rode a pandemic-era luxury spending boom. The resale value of unworn Birkins sold as second-hand online has dropped by more than $6,000 from its 2022 peak, he said. The decline reflects a broader shift in the market for one of luxury's most exclusive products whose appeal and success have been driven by scarcity. Increasing supply of Birkin bags in the second-hand market is depressing resale premiums, according to resellers, industry consultants and analysts interviewed by Reuters, raising questions about a strategy that helped propel Hermes to become one of the world's most profitable luxury companies. Named after the late British-French actor Jane Birkin, the handbag has been central to Hermes' performance. Between 2015 and 2025, group annual sales tripled to €16 billion ($18 billion) while its market value surged. Last year, Hermes posted an operating margin of 41%, above that of rivals including Chanel, Kering-owned Gucci and LVMH's leather and fashion division, which includes Louis Vuitton and Dior. RESALE MARKET UNDER PRESSURE All of that was underpinned by an aura of exclusivity.
